title: Speculative Decoding for Verilog: Speed and Quality, All in One
problem: LLM-based Verilog code generation suffers from poor tokenization and decoding due to Verilog's specialized syntax and underrepresentation in training data, resulting in slow and low-quality code.
motivation: Verilog generation is critical for hardware design automation but standard LLM tokenization fragments meaningful syntactic structures, reducing model learning efficiency.
method: Applies speculative decoding with syntactically-aligned tokenization that breaks at syntactically significant tokens rather than subword units, enabling better capture of Verilog logical constructs.
key_novelty: First application of speculative decoding to Verilog code generation with syntax-aware tokenization for simultaneous speed and quality improvement.
contributions: Syntax-aware tokenization aligned with Verilog syntactic boundaries
Speculative decoding for accelerated Verilog generation
17.19% pass@10 accuracy improvement on RTLLM benchmark
primary_theme: speculative decoding with syntax-aware tokenization for Verilog generation
